verses.text: “As for me, in the first year of Darius the Mede, I stood up to confirm and strengthen him.

Now will I show you the truth. Behold, there shall stand up yet three kings in Persia; and the fourth shall be far richer than they all: and when he has grown strong through his riches, he shall stir up all against the realm of Greece.
A mighty king shall stand up, who shall rule with great dominion, and do according to his will.

When he shall stand up, his kingdom shall be broken, and shall be divided toward the four winds of the sky, but not to his posterity, nor according to his dominion with which he ruled; for his kingdom shall be plucked up, even for others besides these.
The king of the south shall be strong, and one of his princes; and he shall be strong above him, and have dominion; his dominion shall be a great dominion.

At the end of years they shall join themselves together; and the daughter of the king of the south shall come to the king of the north to make an agreement: but she shall not retain the strength of her arm; neither shall he stand, nor his arm; but she shall be given up, and those who brought her, and he who became the father of her, and he who strengthened her in those times.

But out of a shoot from her roots shall one stand up in his place, who shall come to the army, and shall enter into the fortress of the king of the north, and shall deal against them, and shall prevail.
Also their gods, with their molten images, and with their goodly vessels of silver and of gold, shall he carry captive into Egypt; and he shall refrain some years from the king of the north.
He shall come into the realm of the king of the south, but he shall return into his own land.
His sons shall war, and shall assemble a multitude of great forces, which shall come on, and overflow, and pass through; and they shall return and war, even to his fortress.

The king of the south shall be moved with anger, and shall come out and fight with him, even with the king of the north; and he shall send out a great multitude, and the multitude shall be given into his hand.
The multitude shall be lifted up, and his heart shall be exalted; and he shall cast down tens of thousands, but he shall not prevail.
The king of the north shall return, and shall send out a multitude greater than the former; and he shall come on at the end of the times, even of years, with a great army and with much substance.
In those times there shall many stand up against the king of the south: also the children of the violent among your people shall lift themselves up to establish the vision; but they shall fall.

So the king of the north shall come, and cast up a mound, and take a well-fortified city: and the forces of the south shall not stand, neither his chosen people, neither shall there be any strength to stand.
But he who comes against him shall do according to his own will, and no one shall stand before him; and he shall stand in the glorious land, and in his hand shall be destruction.

He shall set his face to come with the strength of his whole kingdom, and with him equitable conditions; and he shall perform them: and he shall give him the daughter of women, to corrupt her; but she shall not stand, neither be for him.
After this shall he turn his face to the islands, and shall take many: but a prince shall cause the reproach offered by him to cease; yes, moreover, he shall cause his reproach to turn on him.
Then he shall turn his face toward the fortresses of his own land; but he shall stumble and fall, and shall not be found.
Then shall stand up in his place one who shall cause a tax collector to pass through the kingdom to maintain its glory; but within few days he shall be destroyed, neither in anger, nor in battle.
In his place shall stand up a contemptible person, to whom they had not given the honor of the kingdom: but he shall come in time of security, and shall obtain the kingdom by flatteries.
The overwhelming forces shall be overwhelmed from before him, and shall be broken; yes, also the prince of the covenant.
After the treaty made with him he shall work deceitfully; for he shall come up, and shall become strong, with a small people.

In time of security shall he come even on the fattest places of the province; and he shall do that which his fathers have not done, nor his fathers’ fathers; he shall scatter among them prey, and plunder, and substance: yes, he shall devise his devices against the strongholds, even for a time.

He shall stir up his power and his courage against the king of the south with a great army; and the king of the south shall war in battle with an exceeding great and mighty army; but he shall not stand; for they shall devise devices against him.
Yes, they who eat of his dainties shall destroy him, and his army shall overflow; and many shall fall down slain.
As for both these kings, their hearts shall be to do mischief, and they shall speak lies at one table: but it shall not prosper; for yet the end shall be at the time appointed.
Then he will return into his land with great substance; and his heart will be against the holy covenant; and he will take action, and return to his own land.
At the time appointed he shall return, and come into the south; but it shall not be in the latter time as it was in the former.

For ships of Kittim shall come against him; therefore he shall be grieved, and shall return, and have indignation against the holy covenant, and shall take action: he shall even return, and have regard to those who forsake the holy covenant.
Forces shall stand on his part, and they shall profane the sanctuary, even the fortress, and shall take away the continual burnt offering, and they shall set up the abomination that makes desolate.
Such as do wickedly against the covenant shall he pervert by flatteries; but the people who know their God shall be strong, and take action.
Those who are wise among the people shall instruct many; yet they shall fall by the sword and by flame, by captivity and by plunder, many days.
Now when they shall fall, they shall be helped with a little help; but many shall join themselves to them with flatteries.
Some of those who are wise shall fall, to refine them, and to purify, and to make them white, even to the time of the end; because it is yet for the time appointed.

The king shall do according to his will; and he shall exalt himself, and magnify himself above every god, and shall speak marvelous things against the God of gods; and he shall prosper until the indignation be accomplished; for that which is determined shall be done.
Neither shall he regard the gods of his fathers, nor the desire of women, nor regard any god; for he shall magnify himself above all.
But in his place shall he honor the god of fortresses; and a god whom his fathers didn’t know shall he honor with gold, and silver, and with precious stones, and pleasant things.

He shall deal with the strongest fortresses by the help of a foreign god: whoever acknowledges him he will increase with glory; and he shall cause them to rule over many, and shall divide the land for a price.

At the time of the end shall the king of the south contend with him; and the king of the north shall come against him like a whirlwind, with chariots, and with horsemen, and with many ships; and he shall enter into the countries, and shall overflow and pass through.
He shall enter also into the glorious land, and many countries shall be overthrown; but these shall be delivered out of his hand: Edom, and Moab, and the chief of the children of Ammon.
He shall stretch out his hand also on the countries; and the land of Egypt shall not escape.
But he shall have power over the treasures of gold and of silver, and over all the precious things of Egypt; and the Libyans and the Ethiopians shall be at his steps.
But news out of the east and out of the north shall trouble him; and he shall go out with great fury to destroy and utterly to sweep away many.
He shall plant the tents of his palace between the sea and the glorious holy mountain; yet he shall come to his end, and no one shall help him.

footnotes.content: The angel reminds Daniel: God set him to strengthen Darius in his first year. Even in exile, the faithful serve a purpose—not to win earthly power, but to stand with rulers when honesty and faith matter most.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Three kings, then a fourth far richer—each rising, then burning themselves out. I notice how history shows us: wealth and dominion crumble. The Lord alone endures.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A mighty king shall stand up. This refers to Alexander—great dominion, his will absolute. Yet look at verse 4: the very moment of power, it breaks apart. So it is with all earthly crowns.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: His kingdom broken into four winds, scattered to others—not to his heirs. Power that seems unshakeable crumbles to dust. Our children inherit what we build only by God's mercy, never by our strength alone.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The king of the south grows strong, then one prince above him. I see how quickly loyalties shift, how the strong are surpassed. God's kingdom never works this way—Christ's strength does not diminish.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A royal daughter sent to make peace, but she loses her strength and is handed over. How tragically human: we offer our dearest for alliances, only to see them abandoned. What different hope we find in the Lord's covenant.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: From her root, one arises to strike back—vengeance for betrayal. Watch how appetite for power feeds itself: each victory breeds the next war. Christ's kingdom breaks this cycle.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Gods of silver and gold carried away as spoils. The treasures nations worship—idols and riches—become plunder. The faithful know: only what is hidden in Christ survives.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He invades the south, then returns home. Each campaign exhausts him. So it is with earthly ambition—it devours its own sons and sends them home empty, even in victory.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: His sons war and amass great forces—overflow, pass through, overflow again. Generation after generation, the fight continues. Only Christ brings lasting peace.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The south king stirs with anger, fights, sends a vast multitude—and it is given into the north king's hand. Anger and force seem to deliver victory, yet the Lord's way is gentleness and truth.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The multitude lifted up, hearts exalted—thousands cast down, yet no prevailing. Power intoxicates, but it does not endure. I've learned: look to Christ's humble strength.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He returns with an even greater multitude. Escalation: each loss requires a bigger army next time. The wheel turns faster until it breaks.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Even the violent among your people rise to establish the vision—but they fall. When God's faithful join the violent, they stumble. The sword and the Gospel do not mix.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The north casts up a mound—a siege engine—and takes a well-fortified city. The chosen people cannot stand. This speaks to siege, engineering of war. Yet faith was Jerusalem's true fortress.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He comes against none who can stand, and stands in the glorious land with destruction in his hand. No enemy, only ruin. So pride enters—when there is no opposition, the conqueror becomes his own destruction.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He gives his daughter to corrupt the king of the south—but she will not stand or be for him. Marriages of convenience crumble as easily as treaties. The Lord's covenant alone is steadfast.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He turns to islands, takes many—but a prince causes his reproach to turn back on him. Shame follows the aggressor. The conscience of the nations does not sleep forever.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He turns toward his own fortresses, stumbles, falls, is not found. The mighty vanish—not with fanfare, but in obscurity. So passes earthly glory.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: One comes to collect taxes and maintain the kingdom's glory—destroyed within days, not in anger or battle. A tax collector, a hollow thing. Sometimes the system eats itself without enemy aid.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A contemptible person obtains the kingdom by flatteries in time of security. Flattery opens the door when vigilance sleeps. Never underestimate the power of kind words to the unwary.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Overwhelming forces overwhelmed, broken—yes, the prince of the covenant. Even sacred things are swept away in the flood. But Christ, our covenant, cannot be broken.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: After alliance, he works deceitfully—comes with a small people and becomes strong. Treachery is his art. The faithful know: God does not deceive.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: In time of security he plunders the fattest places, scatters prey and substance—does what his fathers did not. Unchecked power invents new cruelties. We need the restraint of conscience, not appetite.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He stirs his power against the south with a great army; the south musters even greater—but shall not stand. They devise against him. Devices of men fail; the Lord's wisdom endures.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They who eat his table destroy him; his army overflows and many fall slain. Even the inner circle turns; trust earned by feasting is hollow. The faithful trust Jesus alone.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Both kings' hearts bent on mischief, speaking lies at one table—yet it shall not prosper. The end comes at the appointed time. Evil schemes tangle into knots that God unties.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He returns with great substance, his heart against the holy covenant. Wealth puffs the heart against holiness. The rich often forget God most easily.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: At the appointed time he returns to the south—but it will not be as before. The arc of history bends, and cycles do not repeat. Only God's purpose unfolds exactly.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ships of Kittim come against him—Kittim refers to Cyprus and the western lands, Rome's approach. He grieves and turns his fury on the holy covenant. Earthly power, thwarted, turns to desecration.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He profanes the sanctuary, takes away the continual offering, sets up the abomination that desolates. The faithful are tested: will they remain true when worship is forbidden? Christ calls us to worship in spirit and truth, always.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He perverts the wicked by flattery—but the people who know their God shall be strong and take action. Knowledge of God is armor against seduction. Hold fast to Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The wise instruct many; yet they fall by sword and flame, captivity and plunder, many days. Faithfulness does not spare the faithful from suffering—but suffering does not separate them from Christ.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: When they fall, they are helped with a little help; many join by flatteries. A small mercy comes, but it is mixed—some who join seek only advantage. The faithful learn whom to trust.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Some wise fall to refine, purify, make white—until the time appointed. Suffering is the furnace of faith. The Lord does not waste our tears; He uses them to perfect us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The king does as he will, exalts himself above every god, speaks marvels against the God of gods—he prospers until indignation is accomplished. Pride reaches its peak just before the fall. The Lord's wrath is His final word.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He regards not the gods of his fathers, nor the desire of women, nor any god—he magnifies only himself. Some sins are not of lust or avarice, but of boundless self-regard. The cure is humility before Christ.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He honors a god of fortresses unknown to his fathers—with gold, silver, precious stones. Each tyrant invents new idols suited to new times. The faithful recognize them by their hunger for glory and violence.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He deals with strongest fortresses by help of a foreign god; whoever acknowledges him he advances with glory, and divides land for price. Allegiance is commerce; glory is currency. The Kingdom of God trades in different coin.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: At the end, the south contends; the north comes like a whirlwind with chariots, horsemen, ships—enters countries, overflows, passes through. The last kingdoms clash as Scripture foretold. We are not surprised; we are steadfast.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He enters the glorious land; many countries overthrown—but Edom, Moab, Ammon are delivered. Even in judgment, God reserves a remnant. His mercy is written into the margin of every prophecy.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He stretches his hand on countries; Egypt does not escape. The great powers fall in turn. None stands forever against the decree.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He has power over treasures of gold, silver, precious things of Egypt; Libyans and Ethiopians at his steps. The whole world of wealth and nations bows—and then it does not. Earthly empire crumbles.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: News from east and north troubles him; he goes out with great fury to destroy and sweep away many. Even at the summit, word arrives that shakes him—other powers rise. Anxiety is the tyrant's inheritance.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He plants his palace between the sea and the glorious holy mountain—yet comes to his end, and no one helps him. Readers today hear an echo in this: kingdoms rise and fall, but Christ's kingdom stands. We rest not in earthly thrones but in His eternal throne.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
